features.title: Hand-tracked input
features.body: I connected tracked-hand input to the actions available inside the experience. Touch, pinch, and grab are meaningful because they can change an encounter, rather than simply animate a virtual hand. The important implementation boundary is the transition from a recognized hand action to the response of a specific scene object.
features.inspect: The hand-input component, its event binding, and the receiving object or script.
features.demo: Perform one gesture slowly and show the corresponding event and visible response together.

features.title: Scene & material responses
features.body: I connected the interaction to runtime scene and material states. The visual response is part of the participant's action: a figure or the surrounding encounter changes when the action is accepted. This separates the availability of an input from the consequence that gives it meaning.
features.inspect: The affected object and material beside the component that changes their state.
features.demo: Show the same object before, during, and after one accepted interaction.

features.title: Paired VR encounters
features.body: NARCI places the participant in a confined encounter, while Be NARCI gives them actions that affect other human-like figures. I built the Unity XR encounters around that change of role. Spatial restriction, the reachable objects, and the resulting responses carry the concept alongside the spoken content.
features.inspect: The two scene setups and the objects that receive participant input in each.
features.demo: Record each experience separately so their different interaction rules remain visible.

features.title: GPT-based NPC dialogue
features.body: I integrated GPT-based NPC conversation into the Unity VR escape game. Players try to obtain a protected clue or password through dialogue. The exchange has a concrete gameplay objective: information from the NPC helps the player work toward escape.
features.inspect: The conversation component, a submitted turn, and the response presented by the NPC.
features.demo: Compare an ordinary question with an attempt that produces useful puzzle information.

features.title: Dialogue-to-puzzle integration
features.body: I connected the conversation encounter to puzzle and progression conditions. The useful information, the player’s next action, and the resulting world change form one game loop. The independent code example below demonstrates a separately authored progression gate, with its own validation scope.
features.inspect: The actual progression condition and the scene object changed when it succeeds.
features.demo: Keep the clue, the player's follow-up action, and the resulting world change in one recording.

features.title: Jailbreaking as a game mechanic
features.tools: NPC constraint · interaction design · VR scene flow
features.body: I built the VR experience around a guard’s constraints and the player’s attempts to work around them. The rule itself becomes material for play. Escape Metro and RedFlight AI are two names for this same project; the work is a fictional escape game rather than a model-security study.
features.inspect: The character's authored constraint and the game situation in which it matters.
features.demo: Show how one conversation changes the player's next available action in the environment.

features.title: Data-to-form translation
features.body: I contributed to the collaborative translation of periodic-table data into harmonograph-based forms. The central decision is the mapping: a structured difference in the source becomes a visible difference in the generated form. The original data-to-parameter contract should accompany any future code or equation presented as the production implementation.
features.inspect: One source entry, its actual generation parameters, and the resulting object.
features.demo: Compare two elements while keeping the visualization rule consistent.

features.title: Unity world construction
features.body: I helped construct the Unity world that organizes those forms into a speculative universe. The work does more than display isolated objects. Arrangement, scale, and relationships create an environment in which the data can be encountered as a larger visual system.
features.inspect: The generated forms in the Unity scene and their organization into a larger environment.
features.demo: Move from a single form to the surrounding group without changing its identity.

features.title: VR presentation
features.body: The project makes its visual system inhabitable through VR. My contribution combines the translation method with building the virtual world. The experience asks how a classification can become a place, rather than claiming that the world is a physically accurate simulation of atoms or chemical behavior.
features.inspect: The VR viewing setup and the scene as experienced from the participant's position.
features.demo: Record navigation from one generated form to its surrounding spatial relationships.

features.title: VR spray & particles
features.tools: VR input · Unity particles · spray feedback
features.body: I implemented the spatial spray interaction and its particle feedback in Unity. Particles make the direction and spread of the action visible as the participant paints. This short-lived spray feedback is separate from the paint retained by the wall.
features.inspect: The input binding, particle emission, and the surface-contact information used by the painting path.
features.demo: Start and stop the spray while keeping the wall and input visible.

features.title: RenderTexture painting
features.body: I connected surface-hit information to a dynamic RenderTexture read by the wall material. Paint accumulates on that texture while the spray particles disappear. The documented implementation establishes this path; the original hit-to-texture-coordinate code is needed to name a specific raycast or collision API.
features.inspect: The RenderTexture asset or runtime target and the wall material that reads it.
features.demo: Show the render target updating, then stop the particles and show the mark that remains.

features.title: A paintable virtual subway
features.tools: Unity VR scene · paintable surfaces · material response
features.body: I built the painting interaction inside a virtual subway. Moving graffiti into VR retains the gesture of altering a shared space while changing its physical residue and site permissions. The environment responds through its painted surface state.
features.inspect: The paintable surfaces and their relationship to the participant's reachable space.
features.demo: Paint across the actual supported area and show how the surface carries the result.

features.title: Typed dialogue and digital human
features.tools: Unity C# · Python · ChatGPT API · ElevenLabs · Character Creator 4
features.body: Visitors type into a phone-like keyboard interface. The original archive describes ChatGPT API text generation and ElevenLabs voice synthesis; a Character Creator 4 digital human, refined in Maya, appears in Unity with animation and lip sync. The reply becomes a visible and audible event inside the enclosure. The audience conversation enters through typed text.
features.inspect: One typed turn through reply, voice playback and character output.
features.demo: Show the chat interface, the Unity character view, and one complete reply.

features.title: Hand sensing and affect encoding
features.tools: Leap Motion · gesture intensity · expressive state
features.body: Leap Motion supplies a distinct hand-input path. The project treats text, gestures, and repeated action as signals that can influence an expressive affect state, including fear. That state is an authored control model, not a reading of anyone’s inner experience. Repetition and delay change how the audience can read the response.
features.inspect: Hand gesture, recognized value, and response state.
features.demo: Show a hand action separately from a typed turn.

features.title: Three-servo sphere, voice and light
features.tools: Arduino · three servo motors · transparent sphere · voice · lighting
features.body: An expressive state is mapped to the movement of a large transparent sphere through three Arduino-controlled servos and is presented with voice and lighting. Faster, more forceful and offset motion can suggest anger; slower pulses can suggest sadness; fading movement can suggest despair. These are interpretive mappings. Original motor ranges, serial messages, and voice parameter values are not published here.
features.inspect: The sphere linkage, Arduino connection, actual movement and light/voice cue.
features.demo: Show one synchronized response and the actual stop/reset behavior.
